semantics.note: A retrospective claim about GPT-5: it was overdue, and it fell far short of Altman's promises. The normalised proposition matches the statement.

contract.note: 'Promising the moon' and 'didn't even come close' are hyperbole with no measure. Reading them as 'not the promised major leap, only trend-level gains' is an ordinary plain reading. The result depends on that reading. The packet has no dated list of Altman's earlier promises, so the 'years' part rests on the launch claims alone.

evidence.note: December 2024 report that GPT-5 was behind schedule. Supports 'long overdue'.
Altman's launch claims ('PhD-level experts', a major step toward AGI). This documents the size of the promise.
Altman admits the rollout went badly and GPT-4o was restored after user backlash. This is about tone and rollout, not capability against the promise.
Independent measurement shows a real gain over o3. That cuts against the strongest reading of 'didn't even come close'.
METR finds the gain was on trend, not a break from it. This meets the contract's support condition of trend-level gains.

reviews.rationale: The plain reading is met. GPT-5 was reported behind schedule (e1). Altman claimed PhD-level expertise and a major step toward AGI (e2). The independent METR results show a real gain that stays on trend (e4, e5), not a leap matching those claims. The contradiction condition is not met. Two caveats: the 'years of promises' part rests on launch claims only, and a stricter reading of 'didn't even come close' would be weakened by e4.

semantics.note: 'Would break eventually' is unqualified, so it is a forecast with no deadline. The hedged 'may collapse' later in the post is a separate statement.

contract.note: The plain reading (a sharp, sustained collapse in AI investment and valuations) is an ordinary reading of 'mania would break'. The open horizon is handled correctly, and there is no early rule for contradiction.

evidence.note: Company disclosure: Nvidia revenue up 106% year over year in the quarter to July 2026. No collapse yet, but that cannot refute a forecast with no deadline.
Nvidia's CEO calls the buildout at full steam in August 2026. This is a company view consistent with e1.
Altman said in August 2025 that investors were overexcited. This bears on whether there was a mania, not on whether it broke.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The early-resolution rule (a sustained fall of more than 30% year over year plus broad reporting of collapse) is not met: Nvidia's data center revenue was still more than doubling in mid-2026. Under the rules, no collapse so far is not failure, so the forecast stays open.
